notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2025; AstraZeneca reports in US dollars. Documents read on sec.gov: FY2025 Form 20-F (accession 0001104659-26-019130, filed February 24, 2026) and its Exhibit 15.1, the 'Annual Report and Form 20-F Information 2025', which the 20-F incorporates by reference for Items 6.E and 7.A. OWNERSHIP: Pascal Soriot's beneficial interest at December 31, 2025 was 235,607 Ordinary Shares (including shares in holding and deferral periods not subject to performance or continued employment, on a gross basis). The report states no Director or senior executive owns 1% or more, and the 20-F gives all Directors and SET members together 544,012 shares, 0.04% of the class, at January 31, 2026, so pctEconomic is null (below 1%, not stated individually). He also had 320,854 shares subject to performance conditions under share plans, not included. MAJOR HOLDERS are percentages of issued share capital as notified under the UK FCA's DTR 5 rules, shown at December 31, 2025. They are not updated unless a holder crosses a notifiable threshold, so the BlackRock (latest disclosure December 4, 2009) and Wellington (July 21, 2020) figures are the company's restatement of old notifications against the current share capital; asOf is each holder's latest disclosure date. Capital Group's latest disclosure was December 3, 2025 (4.97%). Investor AB (3.33%) is the next holder. Wellington Management Company LLP's 4.20% is included within Wellington Management Group LLP's and is not listed separately. DIVIDENDS: $4,846 million is dividends to the company's shareholders (Note 25). The cash-flow 'Dividends paid' line ($4,971 million) also includes $113 million of dividend hedge contracts, $6 million of exchange losses and $6 million to non-controlling interests (Note 25 reconciliation), so it is not used. BUYBACKS: none in 2025. The $521 million 'Own shares purchased by Employee Benefit Trusts' in the cash-flow statement is excluded under the employee-trust rule. GEOGRAPHY: Total Revenue by location of the selling legal entity, as reported. The note also shows the US at $23,970 million within The Americas.

footprint.notes: Two employee bases are published and both are kept, as separate metrics: year-end 2025 headcount by financial reporting region (US 17,900; Europe 34,000; Emerging Markets 36,800; Established RoW 7,400; total 96,100), and the 2025 monthly average by location of the employing legal entity (UK 10,600; Rest of Europe 26,900; The Americas 25,200; Asia, Africa & Australasia 32,400; total 95,100). They overlap (Europe includes the UK; The Americas includes the US) and must not be added. The 2025 report says the categorisation of employees by reporting region was updated to align with its financial reporting regions, which partly explains the shift from Europe (37,100 at end-2024) to Emerging Markets (31,800 at end-2024); the two years are not strictly comparable. The 2025 report states 16,900 employees across its manufacturing sites, 31 operations sites in 15 countries (three under construction), 10 global hubs and six strategic R&D centres (Beijing opened in 2025). Sites: HQ, four R&D centres and the Barcelona hub are sourced to the 2025 report. The 2025 report no longer names the other hubs or repeats the Södertälje emissions line, so Södertälje and the Guadalajara, San José, Mississauga, Lisbon and Dublin hubs keep their 2024 Annual Report source (still online); Beijing is not added, to stay within 12 sites. Taxes by country are not published: AstraZeneca's 'Our approach to taxation' (astrazeneca.com) says the territory-by-territory report is submitted to UK tax authorities, so the country-by-country report is private. No U.S. state breakdown is published.
